clue.text: Female singer without one on piano is nobody

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the singer's name wraps round the other letters

parts.note: Cher is the stage name of the American pop singer
one is the Roman numeral I
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: A female vocalist who goes without a piano accompanist is a nonentity.
explanation.definitionFit: A cipher can mean a person of no importance, a mere zero.

clue.text: Salt mixed with hot cream

indicators.note: mixed tells us the letters of the two following words are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A kitchen instruction about salt stirred into warm cream.
explanation.definitionFit: A chromate is a chemical salt of chromic acid.

clue.text: Euro-politician turns up without money in Welsh town

indicators.note: in a down entry, turns up means the word for the politician is read from bottom to top

parts.note: an MEP is a Member of the European Parliament
broke means penniless

explanation.surface: A Brussels politician arrives penniless in a Welsh town.
explanation.definitionFit: Pembroke is a town in south-west Wales, known for its castle.

clue.text: See 22
One Celsius, what, by river? It's colder in here

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
eh? is a way of saying what? when you have not heard
the Ouse is a river name shared by several English rivers

explanation.surface: Someone checks a thermometer reading by a river and asks why it feels colder here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link joining EH and OUSE in a charade.
explanation.definitionFit: An old icehouse was a building for storing ice, so it was kept chillier than outside.

clue.text: Disputing short account given to base camp?

parts.note: a conte is a short story or tale, borrowed from French
a station is a military or expedition base

explanation.surface: An argument over a brief report delivered to climbers at base camp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given to' is a link placing one piece beside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Contestation is the act of arguing or contesting a point, a noun matching the gerund.

clue.text: Badly treated nerd boy had beaten up

indicators.note: beaten up signals the letters of nerd boy and had are knocked into a different order

explanation.surface: A geeky lad was assaulted by bullies.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling hard done by means believing one has been unfairly handled.

clue.text: Nude relation with bottom covered up, notice!

indicators.note: in a down entry the bottom is the last letter, and covering it up hides it from view

parts.note: an uncle is a family relation
an ad is a notice or advertisement

explanation.surface: A naked relative is told to cover his lower half, with an exclamation of warning.
explanation.definitionFit: Unclad means wearing no clothes, an exact synonym of naked.

clue.text: See old flame with a lifetime half wasted

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: half of the word is used up and lost, so only its front four letters remain

parts.note: eternity is used loosely for an endlessly long time, as in waiting a lifetime

explanation.surface: Seeing an old lover again after half a life has been squandered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a verb but is a noun: a bishop's diocese. 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A see is a bishop's diocese, and Exeter is the seat of one in Devon, England.

clue.text: Cure about to come with medicine-end of worry

parts.note: re means about or concerning
med is a short form of medicine, as in med school

indicators.note: end of picks out only the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A remedy arrives with medicine that ends the patient's worrying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to come with' is a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A remedy is a treatment that heals, so it works as a noun synonym for cure.

clue.text: Interlude at centre badly organised

indicators.note: badly organised signals the letters of at centre are disordered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A break in proceedings at a poorly run arts centre.
explanation.definitionFit: An entr'acte is the interval between acts of a play, or music performed then.

clue.text: Nasty sweets — search for savoury items

indicators.note: nasty tells us the letters of sweets and search are messed up and reshuffled

explanation.surface: Someone rejects unpleasant sweets and goes looking for something salty instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link between the wordplay and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheese straws are thin baked sticks of cheesy pastry served as a snack.

clue.text: Ruins a world with canals

definitions.meaning: the verb meaning spoils or damages
the red planet, once believed by astronomers such as Lowell to have canals

explanation.surface: Something spoils a planet criss-crossed by waterways.
explanation.definitionFit: To mar is to spoil, so its third-person form fits ruins; the fourth planet was famously thought to be lined with canals.

clue.text: Ragged article placed outside study, obstacle

indicators.note: placed outside means the word for the article goes round the other letters

parts.note: the is the definite article
to read a subject is to study it at university
a bar is a barrier or obstacle

explanation.surface: A worn-out newspaper piece was left outside the study, blocking the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ragged' here means worn and frayed, not uneven or exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: Threadbare cloth is worn so thin that it is frayed and shabby.

clue.text: Chipper person who's really good -one mum's working under

indicators.note: in a down entry, under means these pieces sit below the saint's letters

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for saint, a very good person
ma is mum, with the 's kept as S
on means working or functioning, as with a machine

explanation.surface: A saintly person has a mother who is employed beneath them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chipper' looks like an adjective meaning cheerful, but it is someone who chips stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A stonemason shapes blocks of stone by chipping at them with a chisel.

clue.text: Salesperson bringing personal equipment may well give evidence

definitions.text: Salesperson bringing personal equipment may well give evidence

parts.words: Salesperson bringing personal equipment may well give evidence
parts.note: a trader at a fair would carry along their own display booth, while a witness in court goes to the box to testify

explanation.surface: A sales rep arriving with their own kit ends up as a witness.
explanation.walkthrough: Read one way, a salesperson takes their own display stall to a trade show; read the other, a witness steps into the box in court.
explanation.definitionFit: To take the stand is to go into the witness box and testify in court.

clue.text: Sw border is needing potassium for shrub

parts.note: the River Tamar forms most of the border between Devon and Cornwall in south-west England
K is the chemical symbol for potassium

explanation.surface: A border in the south-west needs potash fertiliser for its bushes.
explanation.definitionFit: A tamarisk is a feathery-leaved bush that grows well near the sea.

clue.text: Bird, one flapping around the middle of Greece

indicators.note: around tells us the beating word wraps round the letters taken from Greece

parts.note: a beater is something that flaps or beats

indicators.note: the middle of picks out the central pair of letters of the country's name

explanation.surface: A bird flapping its wings over central Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: The bee-eater is a brightly coloured bird that catches insects in flight.

clue.text: Neater rivet somehow binds book that lacks a spine

indicators.note: binds means the rearranged letters wrap round the abbreviation for book
somehow signals the letters of neater rivet are jumbled into another order

explanation.surface: A tidier rivet somehow holds together a book that has no spine.
explanation.definitionFit: An invertebrate is an animal with no backbone, so it is one lacking a spine.

clue.text: Paul acting as a househusband?

definitions.meaning: Paul the film actor, star of The Hustler and Butch Cassidy
a modern male who shares the domestic chores, as the question mark hints

explanation.surface: A film star is imagined playing the role of a stay-at-home husband.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Newman was a Hollywood actor; a new man is a man embracing domestic and caring roles.

clue.text: In the morning unpleasant folk turn up — a bad sign

indicators.note: in a down entry, turn up means the whole run of letters is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: am is short for ante meridiem, before noon
gits is British slang for contemptible people

explanation.surface: Nasty people arriving first thing in the morning is an ominous omen.
explanation.definitionFit: A stigma is a mark of disgrace, a stain on someone's reputation.

clue.text: Period of pregnancy not good- I'm kept in for assessment

indicators.note: kept in means the following letters are held inside the shortened pregnancy word
not tells us the letter for good is dropped from the pregnancy word

parts.note: gestation is the period a baby develops in the womb
I'm gives the letters I and M as written

explanation.surface: A doctor's view: a difficult pregnancy means being kept in hospital for checks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Period of pregnancy' tempts as a definition, but 'assessment' at the end is the definition; 'not' drops the letter for good and 'kept in' places the I'm letters inside. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Estimation is a judgement or appraisal of value, so it matches assessment.

clue.text: Close the loop to survive financially?

definitions.meaning: joining the two tips of a string so it forms a circle
managing to live within one's income

explanation.surface: Finishing off a circuit in order to stay solvent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally, bringing a loop's tips together; idiomatically, earning just enough to cover living costs.

clue.text: See 22
This writer gets to talk with sailor who is a great achiever

parts.note: the setter referring to himself gives me
gas means idle chatter or talk
a tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: The setter gets chatting with a sailor who has done great things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets to' and 'with' and 'who is' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A megastar is an extremely famous and successful celebrity.

clue.text: Is in part of the church office excluding women?

indicators.note: in tells us the first word goes inside the canonical hour

parts.note: sext is one of the daily canonical hours, said at midday in the divine office

explanation.surface: A question about whether a clerical post bars women from serving.
explanation.definitionFit: Sexist describes discriminating against people on grounds of their sex, typically shutting women out.

clue.text: Order cows to be taken to lochside

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle
Ness is the Scottish loch famous for its monster legend

explanation.surface: An instruction to drive cattle down to the shore of a loch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like a command, but it means tidiness. 'to be taken to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Neatness is tidiness, a state of everything being in good order.

clue.text: Irish novelist who's now rarely seen on a train?

definitions.meaning: Bram, the Dublin-born author of Dracula

definitions.text: who's now rarely seen on a train?
definitions.meaning: the fireman who shovelled coal into a steam locomotive, a job vanished with steam

explanation.surface: An Irish author is seldom spotted travelling by rail these days.
explanation.definitionFit: Bram Stoker wrote Dracula; a stoker fed the furnace of a steam engine.
